content:
Connor O'Brien: Heads up for next week’s rotation: can we align *today* on how we’re classifying “load shedding active” vs “incident”? We’ve had a few pages where the only symptom was elevated 429/503, and it’s muddying weekly incident reporting + SLO burn.

Tomáš Novák: +1. Right now people are opening a Sev2 out of habit when they see 503s, but with breakers that’s kinda the point. We need a crisp rule.

Rafael Mendes: Proposal from SRE side:
- If we’re returning *overload-protected* errors (429/503 w/ Redwood overload code + Retry-After) AND control plane + runtime are healthy, that’s **not** an incident by default.
- It becomes an incident if:
  a) internal 5xx/timeouts spike (non-overload codes)
  b) breaker stuck open / flapping causing prolonged unavailability
  c) load shedding exceeds a sustained threshold (ex: >X% of requests for >Y min) for top-tier customers
  d) capacity signal looks wrong (e.g., queue depth normal but breaker open)

Aisha Bello: +1 but we need numbers otherwise oncall will still page “just in case”. Can we agree on a default threshold per region/model class?

Sergio Costa: Dashboards can support it. We already have panels for:
- `requests_total` by status
- `overload_shed_total` by reason
- breaker state transitions
We can add an “Overload shedding sustained” panel w/ alert only when >10% shed for 15m (tunable).

Dev Patel: From support / comms angle: even if not an “incident”, we still need a standard response when customers ask “why 429/503”. If we don’t open an incident, do we still post in #support-escalations?

Rafael Mendes: We should separate:
- **Incident** = something broken / violates expected behavior
- **Overload event** = we hit capacity and shed correctly
Overload events still deserve an internal note + support heads up if a big customer is impacted.

Brian Murphy: Need to be careful with language: “429” can mean quotas too. We should explicitly say “429 (overload)” vs “429 (rate limit)”. For SDKs we’re surfacing distinct Redwood codes; oncall should look at the code, not the HTTP status.

Amara Diallo: Gateway side we’re mapping:
- `429` for “admission denied at edge” when we can safely do it early
- `503` for “service overloaded” when it’s downstream / runtime shed
Both will include `x-redwood-error-code` + `Retry-After`.
If those headers are missing, that’s suspicious and should be treated as a real failure.

Mina Haddad: Routing will also emit breaker reason + state in logs/trace attrs. If someone sees 503s but breaker state is CLOSED everywhere, something else is wrong.

Allison Grant: +1 on using “overload-protected vs internal failure” as the primary axis. Please do *not* create a new taxonomy that requires 12 labels in Grafana :)
I’d suggest oncall checklist:
1) Is error code in the overload set?
2) Is Retry-After present?
3) Are internal errors/timeouts also elevated?
4) Is control plane latency OK?
If 1&2 yes and 3&4 no -> overload event, not incident.

Tomáš Novák: Can we define the overload set explicitly in the playbook? Like:
- `OVERLOAD_ADMISSION_DENIED`
- `OVERLOAD_BREAKER_OPEN`
- `OVERLOAD_QUEUE_FULL`
- `OVERLOAD_MEMORY_PRESSURE`
(or whatever final names are)

Brian Murphy: Yes, but please keep it “pattern match prefix OVERLOAD_” so we don’t need to update docs every time we add a sub-reason.

Sergio Costa: On alerting: we should *not* page on 503 rate alone. Page on either:
- “internal error budget burn” (5xx excluding overload-protected) OR
- “breaker transitions too frequent” (flapping) OR
- “shed rate sustained > threshold” for paid tiers
This matches what we discussed in the last alert tuning.

Connor O'Brien: OK so decision: “load shedding active” is not automatically Sev2. But what do we record for weekly ops review? We still want visibility.

Rafael Mendes: Suggest we log a lightweight “Overload Event” entry:
- Region/model impacted
- Max shed %
- Duration
- Primary reason (edge admission / breaker open / queue full / mem pressure)
- Any top customers impacted
No retro unless something misbehaved.

Dev Patel: Works. Support just needs a signal to watch for escalations. Can we have incident-bot post a snippet in #support when shed >10% for 15m? (no pager)

Sergio Costa: We can do a non-paging Slack notification from Grafana alert rule into #eng-sre and #support-escalations. I’ll wire it behind a threshold.

Aisha Bello: We still need an explicit “when to declare incident” line. Proposal for playbook:
Declare incident if ANY:
- internal 5xx (excluding overload) > 1% for 5m
- p99 latency > SLO + 2x for 10m (excluding requests that got overload errors)
- breaker stuck OPEN > 20m for a tier-1 model in a major region
- shed rate > 25% for 15m (hosted) OR > 5% for 10m for enterprise tier (tighter)

Mina Haddad: I’d avoid tier-specific thresholds in the first iteration; it’s too hard for oncall to evaluate quickly. Maybe one global threshold + “if enterprise customer complains, loop in SRE”.

Tomáš Novák: +1. Oncall needs something simple. If we do tier-specific, it must be in a runbook table.

Rafael Mendes: Let’s keep it simple for now:
- **Pager triggers**: internal errors, control plane unhealthy, breaker flapping
- **Non-paging overload alert**: shed >10% for 15m (heads-up)
- **Incident declaration guidance**: shed >25% for 15m OR breaker stuck OPEN >20m (for shared hosted pools)
We can refine after canary data.

Amara Diallo: Also: streaming disconnects. If we’re shedding at decode boundary, clients may see disconnects. Those should come back as structured error, not a broken stream. If we see raw disconnect spikes without overload codes -> incident.

Brian Murphy: +1. “Broken streaming semantics” is definitely incident-worthy.

incident-bot: Reminder: for declared incidents, include these tags in the incident channel topic: `overload=true|false`, `breaker=true|false`, `region=<region>`, `model=<model>`. Use `/incident annotate` to attach dashboard snapshot.

Connor O'Brien: Great. I’ll update the oncall playbook page with:
- Definitions: overload event vs incident
- Checklist (headers + error code)
- When to page vs when to heads-up
- How to record overload events for weekly reporting
Owners:
- @Sergio Costa add non-paging “shed sustained” alert to #support-escalations
- @Dev Patel + @Owen Phillips add support note template for overload events (no status page language)
- @Aisha Bello sanity check the thresholds and make sure it doesn’t conflict with SLO error budget rules

Owen Phillips: I’ll add a short section to the runbook: “Customer asks if they’re billed for overload errors” + “what Retry-After means” and link it.

Aisha Bello: I’ll also add a quick line: “Overload-protected errors do NOT count as availability SLO failures” (with link to SLO policy). That’s been a confusion point for oncall.

Rafael Mendes: +1. Also: if we do end up declaring an incident, please call out whether breakers/shedding behaved as designed. That’s the key for post-launch review.

Connor O'Brien: Done. Thanks all. I’ll post a summary in channel once the playbook diff is up.
